{{Short description|Sequence of cuboids}}
[[Image:Pad4.gif|right|thumb|Padovan cuboid spiral]]
In [[mathematics]], the '''Padovan cuboid spiral''' is the [[spiral]] created by joining the diagonals of faces of successive [[cuboid]]s added to a unit cube. The cuboids are added sequentially so that the resulting cuboid has dimensions that are successive [[Padovan sequence|Padovan numbers]].<ref name="ubm">{{citation|title=The Universal Book of Mathematics: From Abracadabra to Zeno's Paradoxes|first=David|last=Darling|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2004|isbn=9780471270478|page=245|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nnpChqstvg0C&pg=PA245}}.</ref><ref name="bgs">{{citation|contribution=Beyond the Golden Section – the Golden tip of the iceberg|first=John|last=Sharp|year=2000|url=http://archive.bridgesmathart.org/2000/bridges2000-87.pdf|title=Bridges: Mathematical Connections in Art, Music, and Science|pages=87–98}}. See in particular pp. 96–97.</ref><ref name="mh">{{citation|title=Math Hysteria: Fun and games with mathematics|first=Ian|last=Stewart|authorlink=Ian Stewart (mathematician)|publisher=Oxford University Press|year=2004|isbn=9780191647451|page=73|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xnViTAYeblkC&pg=PT73}}.</ref>

The first cuboid is 1x1x1. The second is formed by adding to this a 1x1x1 cuboid to form a 1x1x2 cuboid. To this is added a 1x1x2 cuboid to form a 1x2x2 cuboid.
This pattern continues, forming in succession a 2x2x3 cuboid, a 2x3x4 cuboid etc.<ref name="ubm"/><ref name="bgs"/><ref name="mh"/>  Joining the diagonals of the exposed end of each new added cuboid creates a spiral (seen as the black line in the figure). The points on this spiral all lie in the same plane.<ref name="ubm"/>

The cuboids are added in a sequence that adds to the face in the positive y direction, then the positive x direction, then the positive z direction.  This is followed by cuboids added in the negative y, negative x and negative z directions.  Each new cuboid added has a length and width that matches the length and width of the face being added to. The height of the ''n''th added cuboid is the ''n''th Padovan number.<ref name="ubm"/><ref name="mh"/>

Connecting alternate points where the spiral bends creates a series of triangles, where each triangle has two sides that are successive Padovan numbers and that has an obtuse angle of 120° between these two sides.
